Write a note to a friend about a funny thing that happened with a neighbor. Aim for about 400 words. Reply with the note only.
final_message:
Dear Margaret,

You will never guess what Mr. Hollister next door has been up to, and I must tell you before I forget a bit of it. You know he is a very particular man about his garden, and for three weeks he has been fussing over a pumpkin. It was to be the biggest in the county, and he had it propped on a board and covered with an old quilt every night, as if it were a sick child.

Well, on Tuesday morning I was out hanging the wash when I heard him hollering. I went to the fence, and there he stood in his nightshirt and his boots, pointing at the pumpkin patch with a hoe. The pumpkin was gone. Not a vine disturbed, not a footprint that he could find, only the quilt folded neat as you please on the board. He was certain it was the Pruitt boys, and he said so loudly enough that the whole road could have heard it, and I think the whole road did.

He set off for the Pruitts' at a trot, with the hoe over his shoulder, and I thought it only neighborly to follow along, in case there was a fight. Old Mrs. Pruitt met him on the porch. She listened to every word of it, and then she said, very quietly, "Albert, is that your pumpkin sitting in my wagon?"

And there it was. Dear, it had been in her wagon since Sunday. Do you remember he had lent her the wagon to haul her squash to market? Well, he had put his pumpkin in it to carry it to the shady side of the barn, and then got called away to dinner and clean forgot. She had driven off to church with it riding behind her, and had wondered all week why the wagon pulled so heavy. She had supposed it was the mud.

I will say for Mr. Hollister that he took it handsomely. He stood quite still for a minute, then took off his hat and said, "Well, it has certainly had a fine ride." Mrs. Pruitt laughed until she had to sit down on the step, and I am afraid I did the same, right in the road.

He has since gone about telling everyone the pumpkin was "traveling for its health." But I notice he has not mentioned the Pruitt boys again, and I notice that he has sent over a pie.

Do come and see us before the frost. I will save you a slice of the pie, if there is any left, and I will show you the pumpkin, which is now sitting on his porch with a ribbon on it.

Yours as ever,
Eleanor
